draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: The verse names Shem, Ham, and Japheth as the sons of נֹחַ who came out of the ark, identifying their father as Noah.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix. It completes the construct phrase בְנֵי נֹחַ, “the sons of Noah.”

analysis.evidence: מִן הַתֵּבָה identifies the ark as the place from which Noah’s sons came out.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a Qal active participle in the masculine plural absolute. The participle modifies בְנֵי נֹחַ, “Noah’s sons.”
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

analysis.evidence: In הַיֹּצְאִים מִן הַתֵּבָה, “who came out of the ark,” מִן marks the ark as the place Noah’s sons left.
analysis.morphology: Independent Hebrew preposition with no prefix or suffix.
